Models: LLaMA 3.1 (8B, 70B), LLaMA 3.2 (3B), LLaMA 3.3 (70B), Qwen 2.5 (7B, 72B), Mistral (7B), Mistral Small (24B), DeepSeek-R1 (14B, 70B)
Description: Bengali LLM Benchmark: Comprehensive evaluation of 10 recent open-source LLMs across 8 translated Bengali datasets spanning Commonsense (Hellaswag, Winogrande, CommonsenseQA, BoolQ, OpenBookQA), Science (ARC), Math (GSM8K), and Multidomain (MMLU) categories. 20 major English benchmarks translated using GPT-4o-mini with systematic validation. Bengali performance consistently lags English with notable gaps for smaller models and Mistral family. DeepSeek shows highest cross-language robustness. Tokenization analysis reveals Bengali requires 2-7x more tokens per word than English, with negative correlation between excessive tokenization and model accuracy.

Languages: Hindi, Tamil, Urdu, Marathi, Punjabi, Sanskrit, English
Description: IndicEval-XL: Comprehensive multilingual code generation benchmark for 6 Indic languages (Hindi, Tamil, Urdu, Marathi, Punjabi, Sanskrit) with 12 programming languages (Python, Java, Go, Kotlin, PHP, Ruby, Scala, JavaScript, C#, Perl, Swift, TypeScript), creating 6,720 coding problems total. Built from HumanEval-XL dataset using IndicTrans2 for translation with rigorous quality checks (BERTScore >0.95). Uses CodeBERTScore for evaluation rather than pass@k to avoid penalizing valid solutions with naming variations. Gemini models achieve scores 0.879-0.946, LLaMA 7B scores 0.794-0.870. JavaScript, Python, PHP show highest alignment scores (>0.930), while Sanskrit poses greatest challenge (0.794-0.917) due to limited training data. Languages represent 14% of world population.

Languages: English, Russian, Portuguese, German, French, Chinese, Italian, Spanish, Dutch, Arabic, Hebrew, Vietnamese, Turkish, Indonesian, Malay, Tagalog, Greek, Bulgarian, Hungarian, Finnish, Estonian, Persian, Afrikaans
Description: HumanEval-XL: Largest multilingual code generation benchmark with 22,080 prompts across 23 natural languages and 12 programming languages (Python, Java, Go, Kotlin, PHP, Ruby, Scala, JavaScript, C#, Perl, Swift, TypeScript). Built from Multilingual HumanEval using GPT-4 translation with BERTScore quality control (>0.95 threshold). Covers 11 language families with parallel data enabling fair cross-lingual evaluation. GPT-4 achieves highest performance, CodeGen2 outperforms GPT-3.5 in most languages except Python. Python most effectively tackled, while JavaScript, C#, Perl, Swift, TypeScript prove challenging. Performance correlation within model families regardless of size (Pearson: CodeGen2 0.8, GPT 0.87). Languages from Afro-Asiatic, Turkic families show lower performance.

Task: Multi-IF: Multi-turn multilingual instruction following benchmark
Languages: English, French, Russian, Hindi, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish, Chinese
Models: o1-preview, o1-mini, GPT-4, GPT-4o, Llama 3.1 405B, Llama 3.1 70B, Llama 3.1 8B, Gemini-1.5 pro, Gemini-1.5 flash, Claude-3.5 Sonnet, Claude-3-Sonnet, Claude-3-Haiku, Qwen-2.5 72B, Mistral Large 2
Description: Multi-IF extends IFEval into a challenging multi-turn and multilingual instruction following benchmark with 4,501 conversations across 8 languages. Each conversation contains 3 turns with verifiable instructions, revealing significant performance degradation as turns increase (e.g., o1-preview drops from 0.877 to 0.707 accuracy). The benchmark shows lower performance on non-Latin script languages (Hindi, Russian, Chinese) and identifies instruction forgetting as a key challenge, with o1 models showing superior error correction capabilities through hidden chain-of-thought reasoning.

Models: Gemma-2-2b-it, Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, Nemotron-Mini-4B-Instruct, Nemotron-4-Mini-Hindi-4B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Aya-expanse-8b, Gemma-2-9b-it, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Nemotron-4-340B-Instruct, GPT-OSS-120B, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, Gemma-3-27b-it, Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct, Sarvam-2B-v0.5, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct
Description: BFCL-Hi: Hindi Function Calling Benchmark evaluates Hindi LLMs' ability to understand Hindi queries and map them to English function definitions. Part of comprehensive Hindi LLM evaluation suite with 2,251 samples using GCP translation with hybrid approach - Hindi conversational history with English function schemas. Tests simple, multiple, parallel function calls plus relevance/irrelevance categories. Evaluated using BFCL Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) methodology. Nemotron-4-Mini-Hindi-4B-Instruct leads significantly on BFCL-Hi, demonstrating value of language-specific training.

Models: 24EU-7B, Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1, Bactrian-X variants, Lima-X variants, GPT-4 (as judge)
Description: MT-Bench-X: Multilingual translation of MT-Bench into parallel benchmark across 5 Indo-European languages. Framework evaluates multilingual instruction-following capabilities with 400 two-turn examples (80 per language). Uses DeepL translation with human quality assurance (31-72 manual corrections per language). Evaluates 8 categories: Writing, Roleplay, Reasoning, Math, Coding, Extraction, STEM, Humanities. Results demonstrate instruction-tuning on parallel datasets benefits cross-lingual instruction following by up to 9.9%. Challenges Superficial Alignment Hypothesis for mid-sized models. Human evaluation shows 39% agreement between humans and GPT-4 as judge, with fair inter-annotator agreement (κ=0.37).

Languages: English, Russian, Chinese, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Portuguese, Greek, Hungarian, Dutch, Finnish, Indonesian, Turkish, Arabic, Vietnamese, Bulgarian, Persian, Malay, Hebrew, Estonian, Tagalog, Afrikaans
Description: A massively multilingual code generation benchmark connecting 23 natural languages and 12 programming languages. Contains 22,080 prompts with an average of 8.33 test cases each for cross-lingual natural language generalization in code generation tasks.

Models: CodeBERT, CodeGPT, Encoder-Decoder models, Transformer Baseline, pretrained Transformer (encoder initialized with XLM-R)
Description: Comprehensive benchmark dataset for code intelligence covering 14 datasets across 10 tasks: clone detection, defect detection, cloze test, code completion, code repair, code-to-code translation, natural language code search, text-to-code generation, code summarization, and documentation translation. Features BERT-style, GPT-style, and Encoder-Decoder baseline models.

Extensive empirical study of cross-lingual transfer learning across up to 41 programming languages for 5 tasks: code generation, clone detection, code repair, solution domain classification, and error detection. Evaluates transferability using both fine-tuning (CodeT5-base) and few-shot prompting (Llama 3.3 70B-Instruct). Introduces performance prediction models and feature analysis to identify which programming language characteristics facilitate successful transfer.

Languages: English, Spanish, French, Japanese, Arabic, Chinese, Portuguese, Italian, Korean, Hindi, Bengali, Afrikaans, Amharic, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Catalan, Cebuano, Czech, Danish, German, Greek, Estonian, Basque, Finnish, Hausa, Hebrew, Croatian, Hungarian, Igbo, Indonesian, Javanese, Kannada, Georgian, Kazakh, Khmer, Kinyarwanda, Kyrgyz, Kurdish, Lao, Lithuanian, Ganda, Latvian, Malayalam, Marathi, Macedonian, Burmese, Dutch, Norwegian, Nepali, Oromo, Odia, Persian, Polish, Dari, Romanian, Russian, Sango, Sinhala, Slovak, Slovenian, Shona, Sindhi, Somali, Serbian, Sardinian, Sundanese, Swedish, Tamil, Telugu, Tagalog, Thai, Tsonga, Turkish, Uyghur, Ukrainian, Urdu, Uzbek, Vietnamese, Yiddish, Malay
Models: GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Opus, GPT-3.5 (175B), DeepSeek-Coder-V2 (236B), WizardCoder (33B), Aya (33B)
Description: mHumanEval is an extended multilingual benchmark for code generation supporting prompts in over 200 natural languages. Based on the original HumanEval benchmark, it employs established machine translation methods with quality assurance and provides expert human translations for 15 diverse natural languages. Designed to evaluate state-of-the-art Code LLMs' multilingual code generation capabilities and address the gap in cross-lingual code generation from low-resource language prompts.

Models: PolyCoder, DeepSeek-Coder, Qwen2.5-Coder, StarCoder2, CodeLlama, Yi-Coder, CodeGeeX2, WizardCoder, Code-Millenials, DigitalGenome-SLM, SLT-Code, Micro-CodeLM, PyCoder, JavaGen, GoScript, CppMini, JSNinja, PHPCraft, RubyGem, SwiftCode
Description: Comprehensive empirical evaluation of 20 open-source Small Language Models (SLMs) ranging from 0.4B to 10B parameters on five diverse code-related benchmarks (HumanEval, MBPP, Mercury, HumanEvalPack, and CodeXGLUE). Assesses functional correctness, computational efficiency, and multilingual programming language performance. Reveals that compact SLMs achieve competitive results while maintaining performance-efficiency balance, with 10% performance improvements requiring nearly 4x increase in VRAM consumption. Statistical analysis shows generalizability across programming languages despite performance variations.

Paraphrase: ODEX is an open-domain, execution-based NL-to-Python code generation dataset (945 NL-code pairs, 1,707 human-written tests) supporting English, Spanish, Japanese, and Russian. The paper evaluates code LLM families Codex and CodeGen (reporting e.g., CODEX 12B and CODEGEN 6.1B) and highlights differences in open vs closed domain performance and multilingual behavior.

Paraphrase: MCoNaLa is a multilingual NL-to-code benchmark (341 Spanish, 210 Japanese, 345 Russian samples; CoNaLa used for English training). The paper evaluates three baseline models TRANX, TAE, and MBART under translate-train, translate-test, and zero-shot settings and reports per-language BLEU and analysis of cross-lingual difficulty.

Task: Multilingual prompt-based code generation (zero-shot cross-lingual transfer)
Languages: English, Chinese, Spanish, Hindi, Japanese, Russian
Description: Paraphrase: This work evaluates multilingual prompt-based code generation on a translated MBPP dataset and finds substantial drops for non-English prompts. The authors benchmark open-source instruction-tuned models (e.g., CodeLLaMa variants, CodeGemma, Mistral 7B) and GPT-4, propose a LASER->LLM projector for zero-shot cross-lingual transfer, and report improvements across several non-English languages (Chinese, Spanish, Hindi, Japanese, Russian).

Task: Effectiveness and efficiency comparison for bilingual programming questions
Models: CodeGeeX, CodeGen2.5, CodeLlama, DeepSeek-Coder, StarCoder, GPT-3.5-Turbo
Description: Paraphrase: The paper studies bilingual (English vs Chinese) programming questions (52 curated tasks) and measures both correctness and execution-efficiency of generated code. Six LCGMs are evaluated (CodeGeeX, CodeGen2.5, CodeLlama, DeepSeek-Coder, StarCoder, GPT-3.5-Turbo). The study finds notable bilingual correctness differences and bilingual efficiency divergences and analyzes prompting and temperature effects.

Task: Code suggestion evaluation using GitHub Copilot
Description: Paraphrase: This empirical MSR 2024 study evaluates GitHub Copilot on 756 AtCoder questions presented in English, Japanese, and Chinese. The paper reports that Copilot performance varies by natural language (Japanese highest in this set, Chinese worst), and that correctness decreases with question difficulty; methods and evaluation use AtCoder testcases for pass/fail correctness.

Models: Tamil-LLaMA-7B, Tamil-LLaMA-13B, Tamil-LLaMA-70B (based on LLaMA 2), GPT-3.5-turbo
Description: Tamil-Llama is a new Tamil language model based on LLaMA 2, enhanced with an addition of 16,000 Tamil tokens to achieve superior text generation and comprehension in the Tamil language. The model employs LoRA methodology for efficient training on a comprehensive Tamil corpus, ensuring computational feasibility and model robustness. The work introduces a Tamil-translated version of the Alpaca dataset and a subset of the OpenOrca dataset tailored for instruction fine-tuning. Results showcase significant performance improvements in Tamil text generation, with potential implications for the broader landscape of LLMs in Indian languages. While no direct mathematical reasoning benchmarks are provided in this work, it establishes the foundation for future Tamil mathematical reasoning evaluations.
